name: PE-22-28

lead: PE-22-28 is a short peptide trimmed down from spadin, a natural fragment that blocks the TREK-1 potassium channel. Some peptide users discuss it for a mood lift, mental sharpness and the confidence that goes with it.

It inhibits the TREK-1 channel, which helps set neurons' resting potential, and blocking it is proposed to produce antidepressant-like effects. It was designed to last longer and act more strongly than spadin; rodent experiments report antidepressant-like effects after short dosing periods, and no human trials have been published.

paras: It is available as a research chemical and discussed in peptide communities as a mood-related compound. No established routine exists in people.
Human safety is unknown. It is not approved for any use and is available only as a research chemical.

angle.text: PE-22-28 is a spadin-derived peptide that blocks the TREK-1 channel and has shown antidepressant-like effects in rodents. Some users discuss it for a mood lift and better confidence and presence. No direct appearance use is documented.

lead: PE-22-28 is a synthetic seven-residue peptide (Gly-Val-Ser-Trp-Gly-Leu-Arg) derived from spadin, an endogenous peptide fragment of the sortilin propeptide that blocks the TREK-1 potassium channel [1][2]. It was designed as a shorter, more potent and more stable analogue of spadin for antidepressant research.

In rodent experiments it has produced antidepressant-like effects after short dosing periods, and it has been reported to last longer in vivo than spadin [1]. No human clinical trial has been published, and it is not an approved medicine. It is categorised in this wiki as a mood-related research peptide; the sources reviewed contain no community discussion of appearance uses.

paras: Spadin (PE 12-28) was described as an endogenous peptide that specifically blocks the TREK-1 channel and shows antidepressant-like activity in animals; however, its effect in mice disappeared beyond about seven hours after administration [1]. Researchers therefore tested shortened analogues, reporting that PE-22-28 showed stronger TREK-1 inhibition, better in vivo stability and antidepressant-like activity compared with spadin [1].

Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, describes PE-22-28 as the shortest efficient sequence, with a very low reported IC50 for TREK-1 and selectivity over other K2P channels; these figures should be read as secondary-source reports of the original study [2].

No studies found in humans. Published work is limited to cell and rodent experiments, including forced-swim and other behavioural tests and reports of increased hippocampal neurogenesis markers [1][2].
PE-22-28 is sold by research-peptide vendors, but the sources reviewed contain no documented discussion of its use by looksmaxxing communities, and no regulatory approval for any use.

timeline.event: Shortened spadin analogues including PE-22-28 reported with better TREK-1 inhibition, stability and antidepressant-like activity in rodents [1].
